cross_market_insights: Every ranking page is written for expats living in Germany or for a foreigner marrying a German: marriage visas, Meldebescheinigung (residence registration), family reunion. Nobody addresses two non-resident foreigners flying in to marry, which is our reader.

The organic top 3 is weak in all four locations: an Austrian ministry page, culture pieces, Facebook, Reddit, a 2011 blog, YouTube and an expat magazine. No German government source ranks organically except germany.info (US missions) at position 7 in London.

Snippets conflict or are unverified: a 2016 page claims 21 days in Germany first; others list a residence certificate; a Berlin translation agency mentions a certificate of no impediment and apostille. The Standesamt, the Federal Foreign Office and the Australian Embassy in Berlin must settle each before it reaches copy. Key research question: how a non-resident couple registers the marriage, and how Australians meet the certificate-of-capacity requirement when Australia issues a CNI rather than a German-style Ehefaehigkeitszeugnis (exemption via a Higher Regional Court?).
Nobody covers the Australian side: Australian documents, apostille via DFAT, recognition under the Marriage Act 1961, passport name change, or the marry-in-Australia alternative.

Venue intent exists but is tiny (castle wedding germany: 10 a month in AU and UK) and its SERP is Pinterest and placeholder sites. Neuschwanstein appears in PAA and ILX Travel as a venue: unverified, do not repeat.
PAA worth answering: requirements of a civil marriage; how much it costs to get married in Germany; can you marry at Neuschwanstein (do not answer without a source).
